content: If you are currently taking an oral corticosteroid, such as prednisone, do not discontinue it without your doctor’s explicit instructions. Abruptly stopping such medications can worsen certain conditions, like asthma or allergies, and may lead to withdrawal symptoms, including weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, and dizziness. To minimize withdrawal risks, your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication when starting budesonide. Notify your doctor or pharmacist immediately if you experience withdrawal symptoms. Use this medication consistently to achieve the maximum benefit. To help you remember, administer it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase the dose, use it more frequently, or extend the duration of use beyond what your doctor has prescribed. Do not stop using this medication without consulting your doctor, as sudden discontinuation may exacerbate your condition. Nausea may occur as a side effect. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that its benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, leading to systemic corticosteroid side effects. These effects are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for extended periods. Budesonide may reduce your immune system’s ability to fight infections, increasing your susceptibility to serious (and rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using budesonide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Prolonged use of corticosteroids may impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. Budesonide may also mask signs of infection, making you more prone to new infections or worsening existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. Although unlikely, prolonged use of this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth. During pregnancy, use this medication only when clearly necessary, and discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Babies born to mothers who have used corticosteroids for extended periods may develop hormonal issues. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has advised you to take low-dose aspirin (81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless instructed otherwise. If someone overdoses on this medication and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, consider lifestyle changes such as engaging in weight-bearing exercises, ensuring adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, quitting smoking, and limiting alcohol consumption. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
